messages:
Laura Bennett: Hey all — need to close out revrec + credits/refunds treatment for AWS/GCP marketplace before we lock SKUs/offer structure. A few open items:
1) Gross vs net rev presentation (principal vs agent) for marketplace deals
2) How to handle marketplace refunds/credits (AWS-issued credit memo vs Redwood promo credit)
3) Contract liability for committed spend SKUs (Dedicated/Private) + usage-based Hosted

Emily Stone: +1. Also need clarity on timing: revenue recognition date is usage date vs marketplace payout date. Payout lag is making Ops nervous.

Michael Grant: And we need consistent language in terms/FAQ. Marketplace agreements can be weird: customer contract is often with AWS/GCP, but we still have our MSA/SLA artifacts for service terms.

Sofia Mendes: For AWS Marketplace, generally the customer agreement is with AWS (AWS Marketplace Seller terms apply) but we can attach EULA / service terms. Private offers add more terms/discounting but still flow through AWS.

Chris Osei: Context from project side: we’re aligning SKUs to Hosted/Dedicated/Private + add-ons. Finance needs guardrails so we don’t ship something we can’t bill/reconcile.

Laura Bennett: Cool. Starting with principal vs agent: do we consider Redwood principal? We deliver the service, set price (in listing/private offer), and bear performance obligations. AWS/GCP collects funds + remits net of their fee.

Emily Stone: My read: we’re principal for the service; marketplace is a payment processor/agent. That implies gross revenue with marketplace fee as cost of revenue / channel fee. But we should confirm with counsel + any historical precedent.

Sofia Mendes: Agree conceptually. The marketplaces usually position themselves as “agent” collecting on behalf of seller, but check the exact AWS MP agreement language. In practice, many sellers record gross.

Michael Grant: I’ll sanity-check against AWS Marketplace Seller Agreement / GCP Marketplace Provider terms. If there’s anything that forces net presentation, I’ll flag.

Laura Bennett: Great. Next: recognition timing.
- Hosted (usage-based): recognize as usage occurs (tokens/embedding units). Marketplace billing is monthly. Payout lag shouldn’t change revrec.
- Dedicated/Private (committed capacity/platform fee): recognize ratably over term (monthly) once service is available.
Does anyone disagree?

Emily Stone: That aligns w/ ASC 606. We’ll need a clean mapping from usage meters to marketplace dimensions for Hosted so we can support the usage reports as source evidence.

Cole Summers: From billing: internal meters are token-based + a few add-ons. We’re mapping to marketplace dimensions in ENG-22111 + PR-19874. Biggest risk is dimension mismatch for early usage. We can produce a monthly usage export keyed by marketplace customer identifier.

Laura Bennett: Ok. Refunds/credits is the hairy one.
Scenarios:
A) Marketplace refund (customer disputes invoice; AWS issues refund)
B) Redwood goodwill credit (we credit future usage inside Redwood)
C) Free trial credits (marketplace promo / internal promo)
We need accounting treatment + operational steps.

Emily Stone: For A) if AWS/GCP issues a refund/credit memo for a prior invoice: treat as reduction of revenue in the period the refund is approved/known, with true-up to the original period only if material (we can follow standard close policy). Also update contract asset/liability if tied to committed spend.

Laura Bennett: And operationally we need to know when AWS/GCP approves it. Do we get a feed?

Cole Summers: AWS provides reports + refund events, but not real-time. It’s typically in their monthly disbursement/transaction report. GCP similar.

Isabelle Laurent: From RevOps side: we can require AEs/CS to tag “Refund requested” in HubSpot + link ticket, but we still need Finance to reconcile against the marketplace report at month end.

Sofia Mendes: Legally: we generally can’t directly issue a “refund” through AWS; it has to be processed via AWS Marketplace workflow. For private offers, there’s sometimes more flexibility, but still usually runs through AWS. For GCP, also through their console/support.

Michael Grant: Also we should avoid language like “we will refund” in customer-facing docs. Better: “refunds processed via marketplace per marketplace policies; Redwood may assist.”

Laura Bennett: For B) Redwood goodwill credit (non-cash): accounting treatment is contra-revenue when redeemed, right?

Emily Stone: Generally yes, a discount / price concession. If we grant credits tied to a specific customer contract and it’s probable they’ll be used, we may need to estimate variable consideration (constraint) depending on materiality. For our size, we can treat as reduction at redemption unless there’s a large credit issued.

Laura Bennett: And if it’s a marketplace customer, we can’t change their marketplace invoice, but we can offset their usage in-product (so they don’t incur future marketplace charges) — is that how it works?

Cole Summers: We can implement an internal “promo credit” bucket that reduces billable usage before metering. BUT that means AWS/GCP will see lower usage for that period. That is effectively a discount (fine), but we need to ensure we don’t violate marketplace rules (e.g., can’t give off-invoice discounts that circumvent marketplace fees).

Sofia Mendes: Careful: marketplaces can be sensitive about off-platform discounts. Credits applied by reducing metered usage are usually acceptable if they are part of a publicly documented trial/promo or included in the offer terms. For ad-hoc goodwill credits, we should treat case-by-case and keep an approval log.

Michael Grant: +1. We should route any goodwill credits for marketplace customers through a standard approval (Finance + Legal). Also document that it’s a service credit applied to future usage, not a cash refund.

Laura Bennett: For C) trial credits: PMM wants a “$X free” message in FAQ. How should we implement?

Emily Stone: Prefer: (1) marketplace offer includes free trial period or discounted pricing dimension (if supported), or (2) Redwood-funded usage credits implemented as a promotional discount against future metered usage. If it’s #2, we should be consistent and treat as a marketing discount (contra-revenue).

Chris Osei: FYI we’re trying to avoid complicated first-month discounts in AWS because it slowed review last time. But we can do a simple “$0 for first N tokens” dimension if AWS allows, or Redwood-side credits.

Laura Bennett: Ok, let’s define a policy:
- Default: no ad-hoc credits for marketplace customers unless approved.
- Any promo credits must be defined in offer/listing terms OR published promo policy.
- Refunds: processed via marketplace only.

Michael Grant: Works. We should add standard wording to the marketplace FAQ + EULA attachment.

Sofia Mendes: I can draft language for FAQ:
“Billing and payments are handled through AWS/GCP Marketplace. Refunds and credits are processed in accordance with the applicable Marketplace policies. Redwood support can assist in coordinating with Marketplace support.”
Also: “Service credits may be offered at Redwood’s discretion and apply to future usage.”

Emily Stone: Another question: committed spend SKUs via marketplace (Dedicated/Private). If customer prepays commit via AWS contract, we treat as contract liability (deferred rev) and recognize ratably over term, yes. If there’s usage overage billed monthly, that’s usage-based rev as incurred.

Laura Bennett: Yes. Need to ensure the SKU definition is explicit: “monthly platform fee” vs “usage” dimensions.

Cole Summers: Engineering note: for Dedicated, we have a fixed monthly reservation + a burst usage meter. We need Finance to decide if burst is same performance obligation or separate.

Emily Stone: Likely same overall performance obligation (access to capacity + incremental usage). For simplicity, we can treat burst as variable consideration tied to the same service, recognized as billed/used.

Laura Bennett: Action items:
1) Michael/Sofia: confirm principal vs agent + any required net presentation language from AWS/GCP terms. Due EOW.
2) Emily: draft 1-pager revrec memo for marketplace (Hosted usage, Dedicated/Private ratable, fees, refund/credit treatments). Include policy for goodwill credits + materiality threshold. Due Tue.
3) Cole: confirm we can tag promo credits distinctly in billing export (so Finance can reconcile discounts vs usage). Due Tue.
4) Chris/Isabelle: add a workflow requirement: any marketplace refund/credit request must have a ticket + HubSpot field to reconcile. Due next sprint planning.

Isabelle Laurent: Can do. I’ll add fields: Marketplace Provider (AWS/GCP), Subscription ID, Refund requested (Y/N), Refund approved date, Reason code.

Michael Grant: Will revert once I’ve checked the agreements. Also will align wording with Soojin/PMM so copy doesn’t overpromise.

Sofia Mendes: I’ll draft standard language + approval workflow notes for ad-hoc service credits. Will share in this thread.

Emily Stone: I’ll use our standard close policy for adjustments + add examples:
- Example 1: AWS issues $5k refund in March for February invoice => March contra-rev unless material.
- Example 2: Redwood grants $2k service credit => reduce future usage billable; record contra-rev at redemption.

Laura Bennett: Perfect. Please keep in mind customer-facing docs: avoid anything that implies we control marketplace invoice timing. :thumbsup:

Cole Summers: FYI we found a dimension mismatch in staging last week (token meter names didn’t match marketplace). Fix is in flight. We’ll make sure Finance gets a clean reconciliation report.

Chris Osei: Thanks all. Once memo is done, we’ll link it from the marketplace PRD + submission checklists so it doesn’t get lost.

Sofia Mendes: Posting draft wording (v0):
“Marketplace Billing: Your subscription, invoicing, and payment are handled by AWS/GCP Marketplace. Redwood reports usage to the Marketplace in accordance with the Marketplace’s metering requirements. Refunds and invoice adjustments, if any, are processed through the Marketplace per its policies.”
“Service Credits: Redwood may offer service credits that apply to future usage. Service credits are non-refundable and have no cash value.”

Michael Grant: Looks good; I’ll adjust to match our standard EULA language. We should add “to the extent permitted by applicable Marketplace policies” to be safe.

Laura Bennett: Great. Closing loop once items land. Thanks.
